messages:
sophie: kicking off a config-only canary for low-touch limit tuning on routing pool 'latency-optim'. 30m window, target 2% of traffic. rolling out changes: limiter.max_in_flight=120 -> 90, request_timeout_ms=60000 -> 45000, batching.max_batch_tokens=4096 -> 3072. canary id cfg-ct-20270320-01. deploy link: https://deploy.redwood/canary/cfg-ct-20270320-01 :rocket:

deploy-bot: canary started (cfg-ct-20270320-01) on pool=latency-optim, percent=2, window=30m. health checks: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, token-cost. Alerts enabled.

ara: noted. will keep an eye on runtimes and tail latency dashboards. planning to check the per-route token cost delta at +10m and +20m.

mike: quick question — are we pinning model versions for the canary or using live routing?

sophie: not touching model pinning; using same model variants. this is config-only (limits/timeouts/batching). pinning would be separate.

oncall-bot: observability subscription created: /alerts/cfg-ct-20270320-01. severity thresholds: p95_latency > 600ms (5m), errors > 0.5% (5m), cost_spike > +15% (10m).

[+12m]

oncall-bot: alert triggered: p95_latency exceeded threshold on pool=latency-optim (p95=820ms). firing to oncall.

ara: seeing the spike on tail latency, mostly reads routed to hosts with async batching backlog. suspect batching.max_batch_tokens reduction increased per-request scheduling.

jen: can we quickly try increasing request_timeout_ms back to 60s for the canary while keeping max_in_flight at 90? might reduce aborts.

mike: if we change timeout mid-canary, how does rollout handle it? reapply a config patch and extend window?

sophie: we can do a patch: cfg-ct-20270320-01b. small change, extend window +15m. doing it now if no objections.

ara: go ahead. we should also enable the routing fallback to 'latency-stable' after 10% error spike for 5m. add: routing.fallback_policy = { threshold: 0.1, target_pool: 'latency-stable' }.

[+3m]

deploy-bot: updated canary cfg-ct-20270320-01 -> cfg-ct-20270320-01b: request_timeout_ms=60000, window=45m. change applied to 2% traffic.

oncall-bot: alert resolved: p95_latency back under threshold.

jen: good. are we comfortable to continue ramping to 5%? I'd prefer to hold until token-cost variance stabilizes.

sophie: propose ramp to 5% in 20m if token-cost delta <= +12% and error-rate < 0.2% over last 10m. approve?

mike: approve from infra side. document rollout condition in the release note: "CFG-CT-20270320-01b — limits/timeouts/batching tuning; conditions for ramp: cost<=+12% & errs<0.2%"

ara: monitoring shows token-cost at +9% and error-rate 0.12% for last 10m. safe to ramp.

sophie: ramping to 5% now. will schedule a post-rollout check at +30m after ramp completes.

[+25m]

oncall-bot: post-rollout check: p50/p95 latencies stable, error-rate 0.14%, token-cost +11%. no further alerts.

jen: ok to promote to full config-only rollout? what's the rollback playbook if production shows tail regressions after full rollout?

sophie: rollback plan: 1) pause rollout and revert to previous config id cfg-prev-20270319-09 for affected pool. 2) if issue persists, pin traffic to 'latency-stable' pool via routing override. 3) open a postmortem and revert to a conservative batching profile. rollback command: `redwoodctl config apply --rollback-to cfg-prev-20270319-09 --pool latency-optim`

mike: noted. also add autoscaling buffer for hosts if we see sustained queuing to avoid repeated rollbacks.

sophie: ok going to promote to full rollout (config id cfg-ct-20270320-01b). scheduling to 100% over 30m with staged increments. change note: "Low-touch limit tuning: max_in_flight=90, request_timeout_ms=60s, batching.max_batch_tokens=3072. routing.fallback_policy enabled."

deploy-bot: scheduled rollout: cfg-ct-20270320-01b -> 100% over 30m (stages: 5%, 25%, 60%, 100%). will post progress updates.

[+10m into rollout]

oncall-bot: minor spike detected: error-rate on one AZ increased to 0.4% (threshold 0.5%). still under global rollback threshold but monitoring.

ara: looks localized to us-west-2b hosts, queue depth higher there. draining a couple hosts and shifting traffic away.

mike: executing temporary routing override for us-west-2b: `redwoodctl routing override set --pool latency-optim --exclude-az us-west-2b --until +15m`

sophie: thanks — keep me posted. if we hit errors >0.5% or p95>700ms globally, initiate rollback to cfg-prev-20270319-09.

[+30m rollout complete]

oncall-bot: rollout complete: cfg-ct-20270320-01b at 100% for pool=latency-optim. final check: p95=410ms, errors=0.18%, token-cost=+10%. no rollback triggered.

jen: closing out. will add a line in release notes and ticket: RD-4227. release note: "Config-only: low-touch limits + batching conservative reduction. Monitored for 24h. Rollback plan documented."

sophie: thanks team. setting follow-up watch for 24h and will file a short post-deploy note in the release channel tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
